title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct Lehigh study settings, from silent individual carrels and historic reading rooms to reservable group rooms and an outdoor wireless plaza.

cards.title: Read Beneath the Stained-Glass Skylight
cards.subtitle: Low-volume study seating in Linderman Library
cards.notes: Choose a seat with a rotunda view for reading or research; fixed and movable tables support both short sessions and longer projects.
cards.short_summary: Historic library seating pairs a low-volume setting with views of Linderman’s stained-glass rotunda.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries identifies the Rotunda as a low-volume study and small-group space with fixed and movable tables and plentiful seating overlooking its stained-glass skylight.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Linderman Library; reservable by request and otherwise subject to current library hours and access rules.

cards.title: Put the Whiteboard at the Center
cards.subtitle: Reservable glass-walled rooms for groups of up to eight
cards.notes: Reserve ahead for collaborative work, then use the whiteboard and extra outlets to keep an eight-person session organized and powered.
cards.short_summary: Three light-filled rooms combine group seating, whiteboards, glass walls, and additional electrical outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries describes Rooms 549A, 549B, and 549C as reservable group-study spaces with seating for eight, whiteboards, and additional power outlets.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms: Rooms 549A, 549B, 549C | Lehigh University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required through the library’s space system; rooms are available during regular Fairchild-Martindale Library hours.

cards.title: Close the Door on Group Distractions
cards.subtitle: Eight glass-enclosed huddle rooms with nearby whiteboards
cards.notes: Select one of the eight sunlit rooms for a small team, and bring markers if you plan to use the movable whiteboards stationed nearby.
cards.short_summary: Colorful enclosed rooms give small groups a defined workspace with flexible furniture and whiteboard access.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries lists eight private, glass-enclosed Huddle Rooms in Rooms 620–634, with tables, seating for four to six, and movable whiteboards nearby.
cards.source_title: Huddle Rooms: Rooms 620-634 | Lehigh University Libraries
cards.access_notes: The official listing marks the rooms reservable but also notes first-come availability; check the current booking system before visiting.

cards.title: Connect the Laptop and Work Together
cards.subtitle: Four first-come rooms overlooking the rotunda
cards.notes: Arrive during library hours with an appropriate display adapter, then use the wall monitor to review shared drafts or presentation slides.
cards.short_summary: Four enclosed rooms offer small-group seating, a wall display, and elevated views into Linderman’s rotunda.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries documents four glass-enclosed Linderman group-study rooms with seating for four to six, fixed tables, and large wall monitors; they are first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms | Lehigh University Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is offered; rooms are first-come, first-served during regular Linderman Library hours.

cards.title: Settle Into the Grand Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Low-volume open study near desks, computers, and a fireplace
cards.notes: Pick a study desk for focused work or use a west-side computer; the room also offers seating near the fireplace and Packer Church views.
cards.short_summary: A spacious historic room supports quiet reading, computer work, and desk-based study in several seating zones.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries names the Grand Reading Room among Linderman’s low-volume open spaces and documents study desks, fireplace seating, PCs, Macs, and a printer.
cards.access_notes: This non-reservable space is inside Linderman Library and follows the building’s current hours and entrance requirements.

cards.title: Take a Carrel for Silent Work
cards.subtitle: More than 50 individual stations on floors five through seven
cards.notes: Head to the north side of floors five, six, or seven for a carrel with its own light, shelf, and outlet in the silent-study zone.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels combine dedicated lighting, storage, and power within FML’s designated quiet side.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries documents more than 50 individual carrels on the north side of floors 5, 6, and 7, each with lighting, shelving, and an outlet in a quiet-study area.
cards.source_title: Study Carrels: Floors 5, 6, 7 North | Lehigh University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Carrels are non-reservable and available during Fairchild-Martindale Library hours; use the north side designated for quiet study.

cards.title: Build a Conversation-Friendly Work Zone
cards.subtitle: Flexible seating and mobile whiteboards on FML’s social side
cards.notes: Use the south side when discussion is part of the assignment; movable tables, soft seating, and nearby whiteboards support active teamwork.
cards.short_summary: FML’s conversation-friendly side offers varied seating and flexible surfaces for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries designates FML’s south side for conversation-friendly activity and lists movable tables and chairs, soft seating, group beehives, and mobile whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: The open seating is not reservable and follows Fairchild-Martindale Library hours; select the north side instead when quiet is required.

cards.title: Study Among Curated Books and Art
cards.subtitle: A flexible community-centered space inside FML
cards.notes: Use the flexible furnishings for reading or discussion, but check for scheduled programs because the room can be reserved for eligible events.
cards.short_summary: The CIRCLE blends study seating, curated materials, art, and digital displays in a flexible library environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh states that the LTS CIRCLE is an FML space where students, faculty, and staff can study or relax among curated books, periodicals, movies, art, and display panels.
cards.source_title: Lehigh celebrates grand opening of the LTS CIRCLE at FML | Lehigh University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in FML’s southeast corner beside The Grind; open study use may yield to reserved programs and follows current library access rules.

cards.title: Take the Work Session Outdoors
cards.subtitle: A wireless courtyard with seating for 50
cards.notes: Bring a charged device and choose a plaza table for outdoor reading or group planning; move inside if weather interrupts the session.
cards.short_summary: This named lower-campus courtyard provides wireless connectivity and fixed outdoor seating between major campus destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries describes Butz Plaza as an outdoor public space between the Computing Center and Fairchild-Martindale Library with wireless access, tables, and seating for 50.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating is weather-dependent; formal reservation requests are handled through Campus Facility Reservations.

cards.entity_name: Bayer Galleria of Rare Books, Room 342
cards.title: Turn an Archive Visit Into Focused Research
cards.subtitle: Linderman’s Special Collections research setting
cards.notes: Contact Special Collections before working with rare or archival material, and arrive with a defined research question and handling guidance in mind.
cards.short_summary: Room 342 provides a documented destination for appointment-based work with Lehigh’s rare books and archives.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries locates Special Collections in Linderman Library’s third-floor Bayer Galleria, Room 342, and offers research access to archival material and more than 40,000 rare books.
cards.access_notes: Special Collections is open by appointment Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., with walk-in consultations available; confirm arrangements before research use.
